hero.intro_en: Write a professional email to your manager asking who should receive your weekly progress updates. You practice asking for clarification politely, with initiative, and you prepare your Capstone content about where you fit.
hero.intro_es: Escribe un correo profesional a tu jefe para preguntar quién debe recibir tus actualizaciones semanales de avance. Practicas pedir aclaraciones con amabilidad y con iniciativa, y preparas el contenido de tu Capstone sobre dónde encajas.

hint.es: Usa el nombre de tu jefe.

parts.en: Context: your role and why you're writing
parts.es: Contexto: tu rol y por qué escribes

hint.en: One sentence. Remind them who you are and what this is about.
hint.es: Una oración. Recuérdale quién eres y de qué se trata.

parts.example: Thank you for a great first week on the Operations team…
phrases: Thank you for a great first week on the [team] team.
As I settle into my new role as [role], I'd like to confirm one thing.
I'm writing to make sure I'm following the right process for [task].

parts.es: Tu pregunta sobre las líneas de reporte

hint.en: Ask clearly and politely. Name the people involved.
hint.es: Pregunta con claridad y amabilidad. Menciona a las personas involucradas.

parts.example: Should I send them only to you, or also copy…?
phrases: Should I send my weekly updates only to you, or should I also copy [name]?
Would you like me to send progress updates directly to you, or also to the project lead?
Could you clarify who should receive my weekly updates?

hint.en: Propose what you'll do until you hear back.
hint.es: Propón qué vas a hacer mientras te responde.

parts.example: Until I hear from you, I'll send this Friday's update to you and copy…
phrases: Until I hear from you, I'll [plan].
For this week, I plan to [plan], unless you prefer otherwise.
I've drafted my first update and can send it on [day].

hint.en: Show you want to do things the company's way.
hint.es: Muestra que quieres hacer las cosas como se hacen en la empresa.

parts.example: If the team uses a template, I'd be glad to use it.
phrases: If the team uses a template or a shared channel, I'd be glad to use it.
I want to make sure I follow the team's process.
I'm happy to adjust to whatever works best for the team.

parts.example: Thank you for your help. Best regards,
phrases: Thanks in advance for your guidance.

rules.d_en: Say exactly what the email is about.
rules.d_es: Di exactamente de qué trata el correo.

rules.d_en: Polite, direct, and ready to act.
rules.d_es: Amable, directo y con ganas de actuar.

rules.d_en: Paragraph spacing, no bullet points or emojis.
rules.d_es: Párrafos separados, sin viñetas ni emojis.

example.subject: Question about my weekly progress updates
paragraphs: Thank you for a great first week on the Operations team. I'm enjoying learning how the team works and getting to know the warehouse launch project.
I have a quick question about my weekly progress updates: should I send them only to you, or should I also copy Maria Lopez, the project manager for the warehouse launch?
I want to make sure I follow the team's process and keep the right people informed.
Until I hear from you, I'll send this Friday's update to you and copy Maria, and I'm happy to adjust.
If the team uses a template or a shared channel for updates, I'd be glad to use it.
Thank you for your help, and have a great weekend.

original.goal: Write a professional email (120–150 words) to your manager asking for clarification on reporting lines.
original.title: Clarifying Your Role by Email
original.body_en:
✍️ Writing Task

Title: Clarifying Your Role by Email
Time: 1–2 hours

Scenario:
You've just been hired by a U.S. company. During your first week, you're not sure if you should send weekly progress updates to your direct manager only, or copy the project manager as well.

Your Task: Write a professional email (120–150 words) to your manager asking for clarification on reporting lines. Make sure to:

Use a clear subject line.

Ask politely about expectations.

Show initiative and a willingness to follow company processes.

Why This Matters:
In U.S. workplaces, asking for clarification is seen as responsible, not as weakness. It shows you care about doing things the right way.
original.body_es:
✍️ Tarea de Escritura

Título: Aclarando tu Rol por Correo Electrónico
Tiempo: 1–2 horas

Escenario:
Acabas de ser contratado por una empresa en EE. UU. Durante tu primera semana, no estás seguro si debes enviar actualizaciones semanales de progreso solo a tu gerente directo, o también copiar al gerente de proyecto.

Tu Tarea: Escribe un correo electrónico profesional (120–150 palabras) a tu gerente pidiendo aclaración sobre las líneas de reporte. Asegúrate de:

Usar un asunto claro.

Preguntar educadamente sobre las expectativas.

Mostrar iniciativa y disposición para seguir los procesos de la empresa.

Por Qué Esto Importa:
En los lugares de trabajo en EE. UU., pedir aclaraciones se considera responsable, no una debilidad. Muestra que te importa hacer las cosas de la manera correcta.
